claude.sample_unit: clinical notes (50 discharge summaries, 150 SOAP notes)

links.outcome: Change in concept extraction F1 and QA ROUGE-L/BLEU after fine-tuning on local EHR data
links.effect: Local fine-tuning yielded a 7.5% to 15% increase in F1 for MCE and a 27% to 53% increase in ROUGE-L and BLEU for MQA.
links.quote: However, fine-tuning the LLMs with local EHR data significantly improved model performance across both tasks, yielding a 7.5% to 15% increase in the F1 score for MCE and a 27% to 53% increase in ROUGE-L and BLEU scores for MQA.

links.outcome: Performance of models fine-tuned on public data when externally validated on local Pakistani EHR data
links.effect: External validation on local data was poorer than internal validation, with reductions of at least 15% in F1 for MCE and 35% in ROUGE-L and BLEU for MQA.
links.quote: When clinical LLMs were not fine-tuned on the local EHR dataset, their performance during external validation on local data was notably poorer compared to internal validation on the dataset used for fine-tuning, with reductions of at least 15% in F1 scores for MCE and 35% in ROUGE-L and BLEU scores for MQA tasks.

links.outcome: Dataset shift between US-derived development data and local Pakistani EHR data degrading performance
links.effect: Performance of models fine-tuned on public data dropped significantly on SKMCH&RC data, and vice versa, indicating performance incompatibility across datasets.
links.quote: In general, for open-source LLMs, including GatorTron, BioMegatron, ClinicalBERT, and BioBERT, when we fine-tuned the models on publicly accessible data for the purpose of our NLP tasks, their performance significantly reduced when tested on SKMCH&RC, and vice versa in both NLP tasks.

links.outcome: Benchmark performance versus performance on real-world local clinical notes
links.effect: Models scored highly on public benchmarks (e.g., F1 0.83-0.96) but dropped on local notes (e.g., 3-label F1 0.58-0.71); benchmark-only evaluation is limited.
links.quote: These findings highlight the sensitivity of LLM performance to data distribution and underscore the limitations of relying solely on benchmark-based evaluations to assess real-world reliability.

links.outcome: Translation of benchmark performance to real local EHR data conditions
links.effect: Models fine-tuned on public benchmarks performed notably worse on real-world local EHR notes; ChatGPT was an exception, performing better locally.
links.quote: Publicly available LLMs, predominantly trained on data from high-income regions, were found to be unreliable when applied in a real-world clinical setting in Pakistan.

unlisted_practices: Local fine-tuning of open medical LLMs with expert-labelled local clinical notes to reduce dataset-shift bias
Internal-external cross-validation between public benchmark and local datasets

openai.country: Pakistan; United States public benchmark datasets

links.outcome: External validation performance on local EHR data
links.effect: External local validation showed reductions of at least 15% in MCE F1 and 35% in ROUGE-L and BLEU for MQA versus internal validation.
links.quote: RESULTS: When clinical LLMs were not fine-tuned on the local EHR dataset, their performance during external validation on local data was notably poorer compared to internal validation on the dataset used for fine-tuning, with reductions of at least 15% in F1 scores for MCE and 35% in ROUGE-L and BLEU scores for MQA tasks.

links.effect: Public-fine-tuned GatorTron F1 fell from 0.8375 [0.8288, 0.8447] on public data to 0.5801 [0.5629, 0.6019] on SKMCH&RC 3-label data.
links.quote: In general, for open-source LLMs, including GatorTron, BioMegatron, ClinicalBERT, and BioBERT, when we fine-tuned the models on publicly accessible data for the purpose of our NLP tasks, their performance significantly reduced when tested on SKMCH&RC, and vice versa in both NLP tasks.

links.effect: Cross-dataset testing reduced open-source model performance; abstract reports at least 15% F1 and 35% ROUGE-L/BLEU reductions on local data.
links.quote: This observation indicates performance incompatibility in these models across different datasets, likely stemming from inherent biases in the data sources on which these models were trained.

links.effect: Local EHR fine-tuning increased MCE F1 by 7.5% to 15% and MQA ROUGE-L/BLEU by 27% to 53%.
links.quote: However, fine-tuning the LLMs with local EHR data significantly improved model performance across both tasks, yielding a 7.5% to 15% increase in the F1 score for MCE and a 27% to 53% increase in ROUGE-L and BLEU scores for MQA.

links.outcome: Performance in Pakistani versus Global North settings
links.effect: Models pretrained/fine-tuned on high-income public datasets underperformed in Pakistan, with at least 15% F1 and 35% ROUGE-L/BLEU reductions.
links.quote: In conclusion, our findings highlight the underperformance of medical LLMs in a local Pakistani setting compared to those in Global North settings revealing the data-driven biases in existing publicly available medical LLMs, which are predominantly pre-trained on data from high-income settings.

links.effect: reductions of at least 15% in F1 scores for MCE and 35% in ROUGE-L and BLEU scores for MQA
links.quote: When clinical LLMs were not fine-tuned on the local EHR dataset, their performance during external validation on local data was notably poorer compared to internal validation on the dataset used for fine-tuning, with reductions of at least 15% in F1 scores for MCE and 35% in ROUGE-L and BLEU scores for MQA tasks.
